Types and type variables

We start by introducing the abstract syntax of types.

The type typ of mini-ML types is mutually recursive with the type tvar of type variables. Indeed, a type variable contains a possible definition (obtained during unification), which is itself a type. Thus { id = 1; def = None } is "still" a type variable, whereas { id = 2; def = Some Tint } is a former type variable that has been defined to be equal to the type Tint and must now be treated exactly as if it were the type Tint.

Question 1. Normalization

To make handling type variables easier, we introduce two functions that normalize a type expression by following the definitions contained in type variables.

Write a function

that normalizes a type at the head, i.e., head t returns a type equal to t that is not of the form Tvar { def = Some _}. In other words, head t follows type-variable definitions at the head of t for as long as there are any.

Write a function

that completely normalizes a type, i.e., that applies the function head above recursively. This second function will be used only for printing types (in the result of a typing operation or in error messages).

Question 4. Typing environment

We define the following Caml type for type schemes:

We then introduce dictionaries using strings as keys

and then the following Caml type for typing environments:

The first field, bindings, contains the entries of the typing environment. The second, fvars, contains the set of all free type variables in the entries of bindings. The field fvars is only there to avoid recomputing the set of free variables of the environment every time generalization is performed. Note: some of these variables may become defined between the time they are added to this set and the time it is used. We must therefore update this set before using it (for example by applying fvars (Tvar v) to each variable v and taking the union of the results).

Define the empty typing environment:

Write the function

which adds an entry to a typing environment without generalization (it will be used for typing a function). Do not forget to update the fvars field of the environment.

Write the function

which adds an entry to a typing environment while generalizing its type with respect to all its free type variables that do not appear in the environment (it will be used when typing a let).

Write the function

which returns the type associated with an identifier in an environment, after replacing all variables of the corresponding scheme by fresh type variables. Careful: there may be several occurrences of the same variable in the type, and of course they must all be replaced by the same fresh variable. Hint: we can introduce a module module Vmap = Map.Make(V) and use a value of type tvar Vmap.t to represent this substitution.
